messages.subject: Re: Bar plots
parts:
Joana,

Is there a reason you're not using geom_histogram? E.g.:

qplot( lengthgroup, data=BSH, fill=catchcomponenttype, binwidth=5 )

Ben

On Fri, Jul 27, 2012 at 7:59 AM, JoSilva <joana...@cefas.co.uk> wrote:
> Dear all
>
> I have issue when trying to group values into bars.
>
> my data is for a species of fish, where I have length, numbers caught at
> length and if the fish was discarded or not.
>
> OurSpecies catchcomponenttype lengthgroup NumbersatLength
> BSH D 142 1
> BSH R 62 1
> BSH D 183 1
> BSH R 248 1
> BSH D 176 1
> BSH R 180 1
>
>
> at the moment my code is working ok but it gives my a bar per each cm,
>
> ggplot(BSH, aes(x = lengthgroup, y=NumbersatLength, width=0.75,
> fill=catchcomponenttype)) +
> geom_bar(stat="identity") + xlab ("Length (cm)") + ylab
> ("Frequency")
>
>
> but I want to start with lengths at 60cm to 250 cm but instead of having
> bars per each cm having for each 5cm so for example every value from 60 to
> 65cm will be aggregated in one bar.
>
> If you could help me out, I would be very much appreaciated.
>
> Many thanks
> Joana
